_comment: Committed metric baselines for the rb-eval regression gate. The harness FAILS if a quality metric drops below its baseline (with a 1e-9 tolerance). These were captured from a run over the committed fixtures with DeterministicProvider and reproduce bit-for-bit across runs. They guard ranking DETERMINISM and RELATIVE ORDERING (regression detection), not absolute semantic quality; see README.md. Re-captured for the W1.0a Phase-1 corpus expansion (12 -> 205 memories, 10 -> 72 graded golden queries): the new goldens are natural-language questions, which today's FTS tokenization handles poorly and non-semantic deterministic vectors cannot rank, so absolute recall/MRR dropped sharply (recall@k 0.4 -> 0.0486, mrr 0.4158 -> 0.0518). That drop is a corpus-composition change, not a ranking regression -- it IS the honest pre-Phase-1 starting line that W1.1/W1.2/W1.4/W1.5 are expected to raise (each such change re-captures these baselines in its own commit per the plan's ground rule). dedup_precision is 1.0 on this corpus because near-duplicate cluster members rarely co-rank in top-5 under noise vectors; a retrieval improvement that surfaces both members of an expected near-dup pair will legitimately lower it and must re-capture deliberately. Raising a baseline after an intentional ranking improvement, or lowering one for a justified trade-off, is a deliberate reviewed commit. Latency p50/p99 are reported but not gated (machine-dependent).
